reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first premise by showing a 63% decrease in T10 and improved stability with increased disorder in the same metal system. E2 and E3 describe the solventless thermolysis synthesis route, supporting the second premise. However, the third and fourth premises about oxygen mobility, metal-support interactions, and Pt stabilization are not addressed in the cited passages, which focus on the bare spinel oxide. The fifth premise, comparing the Pt-loaded catalyst to Pt/alumina, is entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides (Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) improves CO oxidation activity and stability.
A solventless thermolysis route can synthesize high-entropy spinel oxides with uniform disorder.
The disordered spinel framework promotes oxygen mobility and strong metal-support interactions.
Strong metal-support interactions stabilize Pt nanoparticles, reducing sintering and deactivation.
Sub-monolayer Pt on this support will outperform conventional Pt/alumina catalysts in light-off temperature and durability.
